scope: Local operator prediction for the canonical 24 ft, 2500 kg boat and seeded observed SoCal sea. Prescribed saved states and fresh current fields; no coupled predicted trajectory, refresh controller, ocean qualification or throughput claim.
training: Anchor .10 s. First direction uses .15 geometry, not operator or force; second uses anchor velocity and surface rate. The .20 state is a later holdout. Four axis samples train the separable model; two added opposite corners produce a six-sample full quadratic and same-six-sample separable control.
decision: Remain experimental. Full quadratic improves held-out loads but extrapolates far beyond tiny training perturbations and does not establish a refresh tolerance or runtime advantage.

limitations: The .15 check informs the training geometry direction and is not fully held out.
Actual projected coordinates are fitted; nonzero discarded geometry can contaminate a subspace curvature interpretation.
Maximum normalized coordinate reaches 118 and quadratic feature magnitude 7004 at .20; this is large extrapolation.
Initial four-sample setup costs 5.619 s; adding two corners costs another 4.391 s including checks. No amortized speed claim.
All methods use the same fresh prescribed surface/pressure direction, not their own advanced trajectory.
The finite exterior patch, spatial resolution and pressure recovery are still unqualified.
adversarial_review: Independent read-only review found no source blocker. Mixed curvature improves heave but worsens pitch; field residual does not certify loads. Historical four-sample timing is separated from mixed extension and replay overhead.
verification: Final CPU replay reproduced all ten models and both pressure-step loads bit-for-bit after metadata and target-index corrections; py_compile and git diff --check passed.
